title: Pallavi Paul's 'How Love Moves' Wins $25,000 Al Jazeera Award at IDFA Forum
excerpt: The New Delhi graveyard documentary took the Al Jazeera Documentary Co-Production Award at IDFA's industry market in Amsterdam, with the jury praising its political and creative sophistication.
body:
• Pallavi Paul's documentary project How Love Moves has won the Al Jazeera Documentary Co-Production Award at the IDFA Forum Awards 2026 in Amsterdam, announced on November 18.
  • The award carries a $25,000 prize and recognises projects addressing an urgent issue of our time; the film centres on a century-old graveyard in New Delhi.
  • The jury called it "a politically and creatively sophisticated project" and said the award backs a woman director's voice at a critical point in the project's life.
  • How Love Moves is a work in progress, not a finished film: it previously received IDFA Bertha Fund support in 2024 and 2025, and the Forum prize is co-production financing toward completing it.

An Indian documentary project about a century-old graveyard in New Delhi has taken one of the top prizes at the documentary world's biggest market. How Love Moves, by filmmaker Pallavi Paul, won the Al Jazeera Documentary Co-Production Award at the IDFA Forum Awards 2026, announced on November 18 at De Balie in Amsterdam.

The project

IDFA Forum is the co-production and co-financing market of IDFA, the Amsterdam documentary festival, where filmmakers pitch projects in development to broadcasters, funds and co-producers. How Love Moves centres on a century-old graveyard in New Delhi and the community around it. The Al Jazeera award recognises projects addressing an urgent issue of our time, presented in the Forum's Pitch or Roundtable sections, and comes with a prize of $25,000. The project is not new to IDFA: it received IDFA Bertha Fund support through the IBF Classic scheme in the development category in 2024, and again in the production and post-production category in 2025.

What the jury said

Jury members Mohamed Elmongy and Brigid O'Shea said the decision was unanimous. They described the film as "a politically and creatively sophisticated project, exploring the vulnerability of communities deemed dangerous and wrong through state-inflicted violence," and said it would give audiences access to "a place and the people living there who otherwise we may never encounter." The jury added that it was "an exciting opportunity to support a woman-director's voice" at a critical junction in the project's life.

"A politically and creatively sophisticated project, exploring the vulnerability of communities deemed dangerous and wrong through state-inflicted violence."

— IDFA Forum jury, Mohamed Elmongy and Brigid O'Shea

The other Forum winners

The ARTE European Talent Development Award, worth €10,000, went to Stitch by Stitch by Alina Baitokova, set in Kyrgyzstan. The Forum Award for Best Pitch Project went to Parsa Ansari's Shooting Stars; Best Roundtable Project to Daniela Muñoz Barroso's Silence Diaries; and Best Rough Cut Project to Resisting Residents by Nikos Pilos and Arsinoi Pilou — each accompanied by a €1,500 prize. The DocLab Forum Award for Best Project went to Victoria Mapplebeck's This Pleasant Lady.

What happens next

Forum awards are financing and partnership milestones, not release dates: the $25,000 and the Al Jazeera co-production attach to a film still being made. How Love Moves has no announced premiere or streaming date. For Indian documentary, the win continues a run of IDFA recognition for the country's filmmakers at the festival's industry section — the stage where a project's international backers are assembled, years before audiences see it.
